title: CallLint agent discovery index (v1)
description:
The single entry point an agent fetches to enumerate every distribution surface CallLint tracks. Generated from apps/web/data/distribution-surfaces.json by scripts/generate-distribution-surfaces.mjs; never hand-edited.

Each surface's `type` is DERIVED from which SSOT container holds the record, so it cannot disagree with the SSOT's own shape. `status` is the human-facing public label; the internal support enum travels separately in `supportClass` and only for records that have one.

This surface carries distribution facts only. It deliberately contains no risk, popularity, demand or SEO score: distribution channel is orthogonal to a security verdict, and a consumer must not be able to derive a verdict from where a server was found.

schemaVersion.description: Contract identifier. Distinct from the Safe-install bake's `calllint.discovery.v1` in .well-known/calllint.json, which is a different document with a different owner — do not merge the two.

describes.description: What release this index describes. Deliberately not a wall-clock stamp — a timestamp makes every generator run produce a diff even when no fact changed, which would destroy `--check`'s ability to distinguish drift from noise.

surfaceTypes.description: The closed §6 vocabulary, published so a consumer can tell an unpopulated type from an unknown one. `marketplace` and `mirror` are expected to have zero members today: CallLint distributes through no marketplace and operates no mirror. A truthful empty set, not an omission.

counts.description: Denominators, published so a consumer that reads zero surfaces can tell an empty index from a failed fetch.

status.description: Human-facing state. For an agent-harness this is the public support label (Auto-detects / Scan config / Guide only) and never the internal enum, which §20 keeps off human-readable surfaces. For a registry it is the listing state; for a candidate feed it is the feed's role, since §86 forbids a feed from implying support.

supportClass.description: The internal support ontology, present only on records that have one (today: agent-harness). An agent consuming a contract wants the enum; the four classes ARE the contract.
